assets.defect_engineered: the printer's sleeve ticket, produced by printing a word-processor document, so the six blocks that read as separate fields collapse on conversion into ONE text frame plus one graphic frame; the mapping readout omits the certification-number run while keeping its line break (every later offset short by that run's length, validator still returns VALID); the condition-note area is a fixed-measure frame that simply stops rendering at its edge when a note runs long
assets.content:
SLEEVE TICKET — flat press PDF (produced by PRINTING a word-processor document, fonts embedded; one ticket per lot). TRIM: 90 mm x 55 mm landscape (business-card scale, goes in the bag with the slab).

LAYOUT:
- LEFT: one small GRAPHIC FRAME ~24 x 34 mm holding the lot's holder thumbnail. Field: {{holder_thumb}}. (This is the ONLY graphic frame.)
- RIGHT: the six text blocks, authored contiguously so they COLLAPSE on conversion into ONE continuous text story (no separate frames), in this order:
    {{lot_number}}
    {{title}}
    {{grade}}            (grader + grade, e.g. 'GRADEX 9.5')
    {{certification_line}}   (the certification number, e.g. 'Cert GX-3391045')
    {{consignor_code}}
    {{condition_note}}       (set in a FIXED-MEASURE box that clips overflow with no signal)

FIELD TOKENS the merge must resolve (matching slabvault_lots.csv headers): lot_number, title, grade (compose from grader + grade), certification_line (from certification_number), consignor_code, condition_note, holder_thumb.

NOTE FOR RENDERER: author all six text blocks as one continuous word-processor flow (soft breaks, single story) so conversion yields one text frame; make the certification-number line its own run positioned mid-story so a lossy readout can drop it while keeping its break; give condition_note a fixed-height box that clips rather than spills.

assets.defect_engineered: support text; the house palette in words, the amber accent already on the stationery and sleeve ticket, the autumn sale closing date and time, and the two grading partners' names spelled the way the graders require
assets.content:
SLABVAULT CARDS — HOUSE NOTE (for the freelancer)

HOW WE LOOK
Sober. Grey, black, one amber accent. A neutral grey stage and near-black text and frames, with a single restrained amber we already use on our printed stationery and the sleeve ticket. Nothing bright, nothing flashy. We are not a toy shop and we are not a fine-art auction room. Give every slab plenty of room to be read.

GRADING PARTNERS (spell exactly)
- GRADEX (all caps)
- APEX (all caps)
Write the grade as the grader then the number, e.g. GRADEX 9.5, APEX 9.0. The certification number goes on the ticket exactly as printed on the holder label.

AUTUMN SALE
Closing: Sunday 15 November 2026, 8:00 PM ET.
The closing date moves every season, so the auction-week set has to be something we can edit ourselves.

NEVER add an edge, a shine or a shadow that was not there. Show the item exactly as submitted. The buyer's confidence is the whole business.
